seo.metaTitle: Invert PNG Colors - Free Negative Image Tool
seo.metaDescription: Invert the colors of a PNG in your browser: every channel becomes 255 minus its value, like photographic film negative. Alpha stays unchanged. Free, no upload.
seo.longDescription: Invert PNG colors replaces every color channel with its opposite — white becomes black, a blue sky turns orange, the whole picture looks like a photographic negative. The operation is arithmetic: each channel is mapped to 255 minus its value, and the alpha channel is deliberately left alone, so transparent regions stay transparent instead of turning into an opaque block. It is instant and lossless — no resampling, no re-compression, just a per-pixel subtraction that happens in your browser.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Each channel maps to 255 minus its value; the result inverted twice is identical to the original.
Alpha is untouched: transparent areas stay transparent.
Save as PNG or WebP for a byte-exact negative.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
The colors invert as soon as the image is loaded - there are no settings.
Save the inverted result as PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP from the Download button.

faq.q: Why are my transparent areas not inverted?
faq.a: The alpha channel is not touched, only the colors. A fully transparent pixel keeps alpha 0 no matter what its color values are, so a transparent PNG stays transparent and does not turn into a solid inverted block.

No. Inverting is a reversible per-channel operation, not a filter: the result inverted twice is identical to the original. Only the export format can introduce loss, so save as PNG or WebP for a byte-exact negative.

faq.q: What is this called in Photoshop?
faq.a: The same thing: Image > Adjustments > Invert, or a Negate adjustment layer in GIMP. Mathematically it is 255 minus each channel value.

faq.q: Does the tool upload my image?
faq.a: No. The conversion runs in your browser tab, with no server, no account and no watermark. It is free for commercial use and open source.
